title: flo2-calc computation record, schema version 4
description: What flo2-calc computed, from what, with what, and how to check it: the file a design decision cites. Version 4 (flo2-calc 0.5.0, dec:round-2-fixes) adds: the computation SHOWN BACK, as `formula` (equations, plain text with LaTeX beside it, named sub-expressions where the graph is large) and `working` (every node as a numbered step in evaluation order, with its formula, its value and its label), both rendered from what was evaluated; SEVERAL RESULTS, when the graph names a list (`result` in the graph is then a list of ids, and the record holds `results` in place of `result`); the operators magnitude, with_unit (with the `source` of the unit it states), db_to_ratio and ratio_to_db (with `kind`, power or amplitude), count_true and k_of_n; and a new WRITING of values: a whole number in full, a rounded value with every one of its digits, and a computed compound unit shown in a simpler unit of the same size, with `simplified_from` naming the unit it was computed in. A rounded value is still labelled `rounded` and never has `exact`. A COMPUTED record (status "computed") holds its values, its result or results, its formula and working; a NOT-YET-COMPUTED record (status "not_computed") holds the graph, the inputs, the formula and working with no values, the limit it passed and the limits in force, until flo2-calc on a larger machine completes it. A computed record is deterministic and carries no host limits. Version 1 to 3 records still re-run, each under its own version's writing; this file sits beside calc-record-1 to calc-record-3.schema.json, which are never edited.

status.description: "computed": the record holds its values and result. "not_computed": it was stopped at a limit of the host that made it, and holds no values and no result until flo2-calc on a larger machine completes it.

name.description: The record's name. Its file is <name>.calc.json.

supports.description: What this computation supports, as the agent said: free text, or a node in a reflow2 design. Recorded, never resolved by flo2-calc.

arithmetic.description: What exactness means in this record, in words.

inputs.description: Every input node, in the graph's order, with its value, its unit and where it came from.

unit.description: The input's unit as reflow2 spells it; "" for a plain number. Absent for true/false.

values.description: Every node's value, in the order flo2-calc evaluated them.

result.description: The result node and its value, when the graph names one result (or none: the last node).

results.description: When the graph names a list of results: each result node and its value, in that order.

formula.description: The computation as equations, one per named node in evaluation order: every result, and every operation not folded into the one that uses it. Plain text, with LaTeX beside it. A result's line ends with its value (= exact, ≈ rounded).

working.description: Every node as a numbered step, in evaluation order: an input as given; an operation with its arguments by name, then with their values written in, then its value; and its label. A not-yet-computed record's steps have no values.

label.description: "given" (an input), "exact", "rounded: ..." with its digits and bound, or "not computed".

stopped.description: A not-yet-computed record only: the limit the calculation passed, where, why, and how far it got.

value.description: The limit's value on the host that stopped it: the deadline as seconds with their unit ("20 s"), a budget as a whole number.

needed_at_least.description: When it is known: the least the limit would have had to be (digits or bytes).

node.description: The node it was computing when it stopped; null when every node was done and the reply was what passed the limit.

op.description: That node's operator; null for an input or when no node was being computed.

largest_digits.description: The most digits any numerator or denominator had reached.

limits_in_force.description: A not-yet-computed record only: the limits of the host that stopped it.

deadline.description: Seconds per call, with the unit spelled as reflow2 spells it, e.g. "20 s".

pint.description: The version of pint that gave the unit conversion factors.

python_flint.description: The version of python-flint (FLINT's Arb ball arithmetic) that gave the enclosures rounded values are decided from.

content_hash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces, UTF-8) of every other field of this record.

valueText.description: A value as text: a number and its unit ("1.4 mm"), a plain number ("0.3"), or "true"/"false". An exact number whose decimal does not end is rounded to 30 significant digits here, and given exactly in "exact". A rounded value is written as its decimal, in full, and labelled in "rounded".

exactText.description: The exact value as a fraction of integers, with its unit ("1/3 mm"), when "value" is rounded.

design_node.description: The id of a node in a reflow2 design, e.g. "con:cavity-depth".

design.description: The design's id, when the node is in another design than the one the record is linked from.

graph.description: The graph as flo2-calc read it, every input value as text. Re-running a record re-reads this.

places.description: ceil, floor and round: the decimal places kept.

mode.description: round: how a tie is broken.

kind.description: db_to_ratio, ratio_to_db: a power ratio (10 log10) or an amplitude ratio (20 log10).

source.description: with_unit: where the unit it states comes from.

result.description: The result node, or a list of them, each reported by name.

rounded.description: Present when the value is a ROUNDED one: not exact, and never given an exact fraction.

digits.description: The significant digits the value is written to.

correctly_rounded.description: true: the value is the true result rounded half-even to `digits` significant digits (its arguments were exact). false: it is computed from rounded values, and is within error_at_most of the true result.

error_at_most.description: A rigorous bound on the distance between the written value and the true one, with the value's unit.

from.description: The nodes whose rounding this value carries: rounded-class operators, in the order met.

simplified_from.description: Where a computed value's compound unit was shown in a simpler unit of the same size: the unit it was computed in. The value is unchanged.
